verses.1: The Spirit clearly says that in the last times, some will fall away from the faith, giving heed to deceiving spirits and teachings of demons,
verses.2: under the guise of lying liars, whose own conscience has been seared as with a hot iron,
verses.3: forbidding marriage and commanding abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and have come to know the truth.
verses.4: For every creation of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if received with thanksgiving,
verses.5: for it is sanctified by the word of God and by prayer.
verses.6: If you hold to these things, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished with the words of the faith and the good teaching that you have followed,
verses.7: but avoid worldly and empty myths. Rather, discipline yourself for the sake of godliness,
verses.8: for bodily training is of some benefit, but godliness is of value in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.
verses.9: The saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance,
verses.10: for we labor and suffer reproach because we have put our hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.
verses.11: Command these things and teach them.
verses.12: Let no one despise you for your youth, but be an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
verses.13: Until I come, devote yourself to the reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
verses.14: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of hands by the elders.
verses.15: Devote yourself to these things, so that your progress is evident to everyone;
verses.16: keep watch over yourself and over the teaching. Continue in them, for in doing so you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "commanding abstinence from foods" reflects the Greek "ἀπέχεσθαι βρωμάτων," literally "to abstain from foods."
- v. 12: "be an example" renders "τύπος γίνου," where "τύπος" (tupos) is best understood here as "model" or "example," not "type."
- v. 14: "the gift that is in you" refers to the office or role Timothy was given; "χαρίσματος" (charismatos) is "gift" in the pastoral context.
raw:
[1] The Spirit clearly says that in the last times, some will fall away from the faith, giving heed to deceiving spirits and teachings of demons,
[2] under the guise of lying liars, whose own conscience has been seared as with a hot iron,
[3] forbidding marriage and commanding abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and have come to know the truth.
[4] For every creation of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if received with thanksgiving,
[5] for it is sanctified by the word of God and by prayer.
[6] If you hold to these things, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished with the words of the faith and the good teaching that you have followed,
[7] but avoid worldly and empty myths. Rather, discipline yourself for the sake of godliness,
[8] for bodily training is of some benefit, but godliness is of value in every way, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.
[9] The saying is trustworthy and deserves full acceptance,
[10] for we labor and suffer reproach because we have put our hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.
[11] Command these things and teach them.
[12] Let no one despise you for your youth, but be an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
[13] Until I come, devote yourself to the reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
[14] Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of hands by the elders.
[15] Devote yourself to these things, so that your progress is evident to everyone;
[16] keep watch over yourself and over the teaching. Continue in them, for in doing so you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.

---
Notes
- v. 3: "commanding abstinence from foods" reflects the Greek "ἀπέχεσθαι βρωμάτων," literally "to abstain from foods."
- v. 12: "be an example" renders "τύπος γίνου," where "τύπος" (tupos) is best understood here as "model" or "example," not "type."
- v. 14: "the gift that is in you" refers to the office or role Timothy was given; "χαρίσματος" (charismatos) is "gift" in the pastoral context.
